title: A program knows what it does: tests as part of how it works
note: The author's direction (concept a-program-knows-what-it-does): what a program does, looks like and how it meets others becomes part of its working - it says what is happening and how well, in words others can use, and mends by a declared countermeasure, never silently. First candidates: the fulldome reading its own screen (today a job does it, with vt100); every lens saying whether it came into focus (ocoeco check already does).

title: ocoeco says what a lens and a render are
note: Not a protocol beside ocoeco: the shared language and the mark grow to name a star's lenses and their renders (which lens, which format, where it starts, of which data), and ocoeco's tools read, check and write them - so a star outside follows the agreement by using ocoeco.

title: The command line declared with argenv
note: ocoeco's surface (commands, flags, OCOECO_BY, GITHUB_TOKEN) as an argenv contract instead of clap and environment read by hand; proven equal.

title: ocoeco at users' fingertips
note: The author's picture (reflection 2026-11-12-open-source-lacks-bi-and-ba): a user-facing part of the software, robust and not needing a web browser, through which users see the progress of what they use, see what needs focus, add information, run tests and give feedback - all through ocoeco as the unit, format and protocol. First real test of the format: a project outside this circle adopting ocoeco.

title: Chaining: one project's data feeding another's
note: Provenance on every row works; milestones already read other projects' data (device tests); next: declared chains between projects. Settled 2026-11-11: parked: no project needs it yet; it returns with the first that does.

title: Changes in the observatory
note: Each project's changes linked to what they advanced and decided; work gone quiet becomes exact; a milestone shows the changes that moved it.

title: A glimpses table in the shared language
note: language.toml has the glimpses table (13 tables).

title: check reads a repository's essence
note: ocoeco check says how many of the four are told and what is still to tell - advice, never a failure.

title: ocoeco check validates every shared table
note: ocoeco check runs tad's check over each exported shared table with language.toml, so a hand-edited row outside the language is caught before the harvest - not only the row ocoeco note writes.

title: Constellations: stars seen together, a star in several
note: A constellation is a place of its own: it keeps what holds between its stars and what is decided for them together, and gathers their data; its fulldome is the same outermost lens over all of it. The mark says what a place gathers - many to many, replacing the single parent. First: OCO itself as a constellation, with ocoeco, oco-agent and tad as its stars. Order decided 2026-11-12: after the first lenses. The mark's parent and kind are read in about eighteen places in ocoeco and sixty in the observatory engine's hand-written views - the very views lenses replace; changing them first would be work done twice.

title: The core moved into ocoeco
note: The mark, discovery and the harvest live here as the ocoeco crate and command; the observatory gathers with it; the engine is only the face.

title: Declare the relations, and check them across projects
note: First, because the fulldome's continuity rests on it (the-fulldome-lens-by-lens). The shared language says which field refers to which table - research, sources, decided, advances, touches, serves, answers, project/table:id across stars - and gains the relations found missing: a decision refining or replacing another (written as text three times on 2026-11-12), and work serving a milestone or decision. ocoeco check, over every star, verifies every link. 2026-11-12: the check found 15 links leading nowhere across 22 stars, not the 2 a rough count had: 7 written by ocoeco's own glimpse (milestone: for the table milestones - fixed in the tool and in the data), 8 decisions in the phone's lab about milestones kept in another star (now naming it). A milestone's criteria are links too (declared). All stars' links now hold. Correction, 2026-11-12: the sentence above - all stars' links now hold - was written into the job before its last check had run, and that check said otherwise: declaring a milestone's criteria as plain links misread 45 conditions (feature:name@level) as broken. Criteria now pass those over. Checked after that, by ocoeco check --root over every star: 17 link(s) lead nowhere, in git-rhizoid/git-rhizoid.github.io (1) linux-phone-oco/docs (16). A conclusion is written from what the check counted, never before it. Counted 2026-11-12 by ocoeco check --root over 22 stars, after conditions (anything with an @ in a milestone's criteria) were told from links and rhizcut was recorded in Rhizoid: 0 link(s) lead nowhere. Counted again 2026-11-12, this time with every star on its main (the count before read the lab's copies as they stood, one of them on a branch Rhizoid's check had refused - its pages had not been rendered again): 0 link(s) lead nowhere across 22 stars. Done 2026-11-12: thirteen relations declared and held by the lenses; every link in every star leads somewhere. What a place gathers moves to constellations, after the first lenses.

title: Every project gathers by itself
note: The principle lived: no project's data kept by hand.

title: The formats and protocols
note: tad (text as data) is the format ocoeco speaks: tables as JSON lines with a schema, canonical form, verification; the mark; to be specified here. Specified in SPEC.md (version 1).

title: Gathered data on its own branch; automation is not work
note: The gatherer committed to the default branch and then counted its own commits as activity, and a protected branch refused it. Now: the oco-data branch, path@branch in the mark, bots' and workflows' commits left out of activity; the marks of every repository to follow. Settled 2026-11-11: gatherers write to an oco-data branch in every marked project.

title: Gatherers: data made by work
note: Standard gatherers for activity, releases and CI: one reusable workflow, a five-line caller, running daily in all eleven marked repositories and written into each one's own oco/gathered/.

title: Test results as a standard gatherer
note: Device and project test runs gathered the same way everywhere (today: devlab writes them for surya).

title: The session log and timed manual work, from glimpses
note: Later, with care: a day's session log rendered from its glimpses, and timed manual work as glimpses with effort - one stream instead of three, without breaking the observatory's views.

title: Hand-work saturation: the table, the command, the views, land
note: Live 2026-11-11: the table, ocoeco hand (match, bump, or ask), the views (a page per project; hand-work worth a tool in the attention view, summed across projects), and land asking for --hand or --no-hand - a failure to record stops the landing.

title: harvest and discover become observe
note: 2026-11-12: the command is ocoeco observe, harvest kept as its alias; it observes what has run too. Done 2026-11-12: ocoeco observe gathers the places' tables and what has run there, at every scale - by GitHub's search (the observatory) or the places a machine holds (--root); harvest stays as its alias, and the observatory's workflow calls observe. ocoeco discover remains, as the way to list what would be found.
next: the observatory's workflow calls ocoeco observe; discover folds into observe

title: A finding says how it is known
note: Research rows gain how each finding is known - measured, read, or reasoned - so a guess never stands as a fact (2026-11-12: a reasoned cause of the stall was wrong); results gain evidence as a link to what proves it. Close to what Truelink is for.

title: Joining in one command
note: ocoeco init writes a repository's mark, the gatherer's caller and a place for its records (never overwriting); ocoeco check reads the repository as the harvest would. Fifteen repositories had been joined by hand-written scripts.

title: land and CI refuse a change with no record
note: land refuses; a reusable CI check from ocoeco fails a pull request without one; ocoeco hooks installs a local hook that points to ocoeco commit. Bots (feeds, update-pins, harvest) record through ocoeco commit too; dependency bumps get their record from the check's own exemption list.

title: Languages specified
note: SPEC section 9: the interface in Fluent catalogs, the data in each project's own translations table (by human or machine), applied only to that project's rows.

title: A lens declared as data, made real on one star
note: A lens, with its two faces: a glimpse (the data's place, relations, and how it is entered with ease) and a focus (queries, and how what they bring into focus is laid out). The shared language's tables (language.toml) and relations (relations.toml) are regrouped as the glimpses of the core lenses. ocoeco glimpse is composed from them with argenv - collisions found at build - and opens a composed view with no arguments; ocoeco note gives way to it; ocoeco focus runs a lens. Built once, on one star, with both faces, before it is generalized. To settle then: the name of the table of work done, now that glimpse is the general word. 2026-11-12: the work lens's focus is data and equals the hand-written board byte for byte on every star's main (decision 2026-11-12-a-focus-is-data). ocoeco now builds on tad 0.5.0, for its SQL. Correction, 2026-11-12: the landing recorded above carried only the record. To make its proof the job brought every star to its main - ocoeco among them - which wiped every change to files that already existed (the module's place in the library, the command, the lens's focus parts, the move to tad 0.5.0); only the new file survived, unused. The proof ran from the program built before that, and was true, but main did not hold what was proven. Found the same day when the next step would not build. Landed again here, proven again, with the format check CI runs, and main itself read after landing to see that it holds the code. ocoeco board is now the work lens focused on every place; its hand-written view is removed; its last line says stars - one word changed in the lens, none in the program. 2026-11-12: the work lens has its glimpse: an entry is declared in the lens - what is asked, what the computer supplies and when (new, always, FIELD changes, FIELD becomes VALUE). ocoeco glimpse alone shows every entry of every lens; two entries with one name stop the build. 2026-11-12: every lens has its glimpse - eleven entries; the computer supplies the date and who. Used for real: today's session was recorded through the session entry. 2026-11-12: the fulldome opens in a terminal (ocoeco fulldome): every lens, what each brings into focus, what can be glimpsed through it. Proven in a real terminal with keys pressed. 2026-11-12: the dome is the port, surfaces its adapters (decision 2026-11-12-the-dome-is-the-port); Markdown is the second surface, on lenses written before it. 2026-11-12: the HTML and CSS surface, and the fulldome laid out whole on any surface; published by the observatory as fulldome.html.
next: the five lenses without a focus get one, so the fulldome can stand where the engine's views do; and an entry filled inside the terminal
